newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia Aeroflot says plans buy 10 Boeing 737s.
newsitem.headline: Russia Aeroflot says plans buy 10 Boeing 737s.

text.p: Aeroflot-Russian International Airlines plans to buy 10 Boeing 737-400 passenger jets in 1997-98, paying for them over an extended period, deputy chief executive Valery Okulov said on Tuesday.
"We plan to operate these jets on routes of up to 3,000 km from Russia to Europe and we plan to develop our route network in Russia and the CIS as well," Okulov told Reuters.
He said a letter of intent was signed on September 3 at the Farnborough international air show in Britain.
"We want to replace our Tupolev 134s," said Okulov, referring to a short or medium haul Russian-made jet.

He declined to give details of the cost of the deal, involving new planes direct from the Boeing plant, or of the extended payments scheme. However, he noted that the average price for a 737-400 was $25-30 million.
State-owned Aeroflot inherited its international routes from the former Soviet monopoly carrier, which broke up when the Soviet Union collapsed.
It operates 18 Russian-made Ilyushin-86, six Ilyushin-96-300 and 27 Ilyushin-62 long-range jets, 29 Tupolev-154 and 13 Tupolev-134 medium-range planes.
It leases two Boeing-767 and 10 Airbus A-310 long-range jets, of which four were added in August.
Aeroflot flies to 126 international destinations in 102 countries, including Commonwealth of Independent States member countries. They have recently begun flying eight routes in Russia.
